97.0.0.en: 1- The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice; let the multitude of isles be glad thereof.

97.0.1.en: 1- The Lord is King over the earth because He is its Creator, and He is King from eternity, but He is King also in the fullness of time when He was lifted up on the Cross, and then the earth rejoiced, that is, mankind, at His salvation, which freed them from bondage to sin and opened to them the door of paradise.

97.0.2.en: 2- The many isles are the churches of the New Testament, which have spread throughout the whole world. And the isles are firm like the churches that are firm in the faith, and surrounded by the sea on every side, which symbolizes the world. So the isles are strong by Christ who dwells in them, even if the world surrounds them with all its evils on every side.

97.1.0.en: 2- Clouds and darkness are round about him: righteousness and judgment are the habitation of his throne.

97.1.1.en: 1- The cloud and the mist are around God because He is great and awesome and His depths cannot be comprehended, just as what is behind the mist and the cloud cannot be seen. The mist has appeared around God many times in the Old and New Testaments: it would settle around the tabernacle of meeting, and the pillar of cloud led the people of God in the wilderness; the mist also appeared on the mountain when Moses was given the commandments and the Law, and the mist also appeared at the Transfiguration of Christ … The cloud and the mist symbolize the body of Christ, in which He hid His divinity. And the Virgin is the cloud that carried Christ in her womb, as Isaiah mentioned (Isa 19:1). The angels also are the cloud and the mist surrounding God, and likewise the believers in God are the cloud and the mist by their deep, luminous lives, bearing witness to God by their conduct.

97.1.2.en: 2- And God also has perfect justice, and therefore judgment and condemnation belong to Him alone. By His Incarnation He condemned sin when He was crucified for us, and at His second coming He will judge and condemn the whole world. And the believers in God in their lives show His justice and His judgment, for they are a light to the world, calling others to repent and follow their example, otherwise they will be judged before God.

97.2.0.en: 3- A fire goeth before him, and burneth up his enemies round about.

97.2.1.en: Fire goes before God to declare His power, for He is a consuming fire that punishes the wicked and destroys them on the last day, that is, in eternal torment. Fire also purifies those who believe in Him and burns up their sins. Likewise the divine fire kindles love in the hearts of His servants, as the Holy Spirit descended as tongues of fire on the heads of the Apostles gathered in the upper room on the day of Pentecost, and drove them by love to preach to the whole world. Fire may also symbolize the angels who prepare the way of God, and also John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Christ by proclaiming the truth and calling the crowds to baptism and to change their lives.

97.3.0.en: 4- His lightnings enlightened the world: the earth saw, and trembled.

97.3.1.en: 1- Lightning shines and appears to the whole world, for it flashes from the east and reaches to the west, and it symbolizes the redemption of Christ and the preaching of the Apostles and all the ministries offered to this day, for they enlighten the hearts of believers and draw them to God to live with Him. But the wicked, who are symbolized by the earth because their thoughts are earthly and carnal, do not obey and submit to the light of God, but it exposes their sins and they tremble and do not return to Him.

97.3.2.en: 2- Lightnings also symbolize the promises of God, which must be fulfilled, and they are bright and give hope to man, and lightning is followed by the falling of rain, which symbolizes heavenly blessings.

97.4.0.en: 5- The hills melted like wax at the presence of the LORD, at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.

97.4.1.en: 1- The mountains that melt easily like wax before the face of the Lord, who is Lord of the whole earth, are the Roman Empire, which turned to Christianity not only as individuals but also its head, King Constantine, who permitted freedom of the Christian religion and the turning of the pagan temples into churches. The Roman Empire symbolizes the authorities and powers in the world, which God turns and subjects to Himself, just as the Soviet Union collapsed in the present generation and the authority of Communism weakened, so that Christian worship returned to the churches there.

97.4.2.en: 2- The mountains also symbolize the forces of evil, which fear the power of God, Lord of the whole earth, and melt and have no existence or power before Him, and this of course reassures the believers, so that they do not fear the wicked.

97.5.0.en: 6- The heavens declare his righteousness, and all the people see his glory.

97.5.1.en: 1- The heavens declared the justice of God, who comes to take away the sins of the world and free mankind by His Incarnation, through the announcement of the angels that Christ was born, so the shepherds rejoiced and went to the manger; and the heavens also declared His justice when He was baptized in the Jordan River by John the Baptist, and heaven bore witness to Him that He is the beloved Son (Mt 3:17).

97.5.2.en: 2- All the peoples saw the glory of God through the preaching of the Apostles of the redemption and Resurrection of Christ, and many of the Gentiles believed.

97.5.3.en: May all the movements of nature and the events of life that show the fear of God call you to repent and keep away from sin, so that you draw near to God and are enlightened by His light through prayer and reading His word.

97.6.s.en: (2) The Lord exalted above the gods

97.6.0.en: 7- Confounded be all they that serve graven images, that boast themselves of idols: worship him, all ye gods.

97.6.1.en: 1- When God is glorified and all creation submits to Him, those who worship idols and boast of them feel that they are in shame, for their pagan gods appear very weak before God. So also everyone who relies on and clings to the material things of the world and its lusts, and every power in it, feels that he is nothing before the power of God, and is put to shame, especially when he loses this power, such as money, health or relationships, and God alone remains the strong One, able to do all things.

97.6.2.en: 2- When the glory of God appears, not only the human beings who believe in Him submit to Him, but also the gods, who are the angels, and they glorify Him. And the demons also, who work in the idols, cannot stand before the power of God, as the weakness of the god Bel appeared before the power of God in His prophet Daniel (Additions to Daniel 3:

97.7.0.en: 8- Zion heard, and was glad; and the daughters of Judah rejoiced because of thy judgments, O LORD.

97.7.1.en: When the gods, that is, the angels, worshiped God, and Zion heard, and also the daughters of Judah, that is, the believers in God, they rejoiced and exulted and praised God, because He is the true God and not the idols. If the pagans bow down and boast of the idols, the believers in the Old or New Testament rejoice and exult and glorify God.

97.8.0.en: 9- For thou, LORD, art high above all the earth: thou art exalted far above all gods.

97.8.1.en: 1- The psalmist declares that God is higher than all the pagan gods that the Gentiles worship, that is, that He is the only God, and He is above all the powers and material things with which the people of the world are occupied, because He is the Creator of all. Therefore He ought to be exalted in the hearts of men above everything else, so that they worship Him faithfully with all their hearts.

97.8.2.en: 2- When Christ was lifted up on the Cross He became higher than the powers of Satan when He died, and Satan was bound, and His love, which surpasses all understanding, appeared, and the Jews and the Gentiles were called to salvation by faith in Him.

97.8.3.en: Always remember your only goal in life, which is the love of God and eternity, so that you always strive toward Him and leave behind everything that hinders you from Him, and so grow quietly in His love and advance toward blessed eternity.

97.9.s.en: (3) The joy of the righteous in the Lord

97.9.0.en: 10- Ye that love the LORD, hate evil: he preserveth the souls of his saints; he delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.

97.9.1.en: 1- Whoever loves the Lord must hate evil, because the love of the Lord cannot agree with the love of evil, and hatred of evil is considered a virtue, because it means love of righteousness.

97.9.2.en: 2- God blesses those who love Him with two things:

97.9.3.en: a- He preserves their lives from evil, though not from the pains of this life, and gives them peace during trials, and then eternal life.

97.9.4.en: b- He delivers them from the wicked, that is, the demons, so that they do not have dominion over them, and He nullifies their wars and exposes their deceit, so that those who love the Lord do not fall into the deceit of the demons.

97.10.0.en: 11- Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.

97.10.1.en: 1- Among the blessings that God gives to His righteous lovers is that He enlightens their lives to know Him and sows this knowledge in the depths of their hearts so that they remain firm in Him, and from this enlightenment comes a joy that lasts in their lives as long as they hold fast to uprightness of heart.

97.10.2.en: 2- The light that is sown for the righteous is Christ our God, who became incarnate in the fullness of time and gave them salvation. And from this salvation came joy in all their lives, because their hearts are upright before Him.

97.10.3.en: 3- The light that is sown for the righteous is the Holy Bible, that they may eat of it and be satisfied, and their upright hearts rejoice at all times and forever.

97.11.0.en: 12- Rejoice in the LORD, ye righteous; and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.

97.11.1.en: 1- This verse is a call to the righteous to rejoice in the knowledge of God and His salvation, and not in the lusts of the world, and also to rejoice in the faith of many and their enjoyment of the salvation of Christ.

97.11.2.en: 2- The righteous express their joy by thanking God and praising Him, so they mention His holy name often to enjoy Him, and thank Him for all His gifts, and contemplate His gracious person and His holiness, and so they live in heaven while they are on earth.

97.11.3.en: Seek Christ in prayer and meditation so that you may be satisfied with Him and be repelled by sin and all that causes it, and then you will remain firm in the love of God and His commandments.

97.11.4.en: Joy in salvation. Psalm “O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things” .. v. 1 Introduction:

97.11.5.en: 1- Its author: there are two opinions:

97.11.6.en: a- It is one of the orphan psalms, in whose title there is no name of the author.

97.11.7.en: b- In the title of this psalm in the Septuagint it is said to be David’s.

97.11.9.en: a- To glorify God, who gave salvation by the hand of David through his victory over the nations surrounding the Jews.

97.11.10.en: b- It may be a prophecy of the return from the captivity, deliverance from its bondage, and the rebuilding of the Temple.

97.11.11.en: c- It is a prophecy of the salvation of Christ, who became incarnate in the fullness of time and gave salvation by His Cross.

97.11.12.en: 3- This psalm is the only psalm whose title is “A Psalm,” and the word psalm means that it was sung with the accompaniment of a musical instrument, which is the pipe.

97.11.13.en: 4- This psalm is among the royal psalms, which we said before are (Ps 95-Ps 100), in addition to (Ps 93), which is a preparation for them.

97.11.14.en: 5- There is a similarity between this psalm and Psalm 96, for both speak of the Lord the King and His praise.

97.11.15.en: 6- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Agpeya, in the prayer of the Ninth Hour, in which Christ completed redemption by His death on the Cross, so He reigned on the wood of the Cross, and over the hearts of His children to whom He gave salvation.

98.0.s.en: (1) Joy in the salvation of God

98.0.0.en: 1- O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.

98.0.1.en: 1- David the prophet calls all the believers to sing to the Lord a new song to thank Him and praise Him for His wonders that He did with His people in the Old Testament, and then in the New Testament, and which were completed by the wonder of the Cross, in which He offered salvation to everyone who believes in Him in the whole world.

98.0.2.en: 2- The salvation that Christ offered on the Cross He accomplished by His right hand, that is, His power, and His arm, that is, the only-begotten Son incarnate, as Isaiah the prophet pointed to this (Isa 51:9; 53:1). The right hand and the arm also symbolize the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church. In sum, Christ bore our sins alone on the Cross, and died and raised Himself by the power of His divinity.

98.1.0.en: 2- The LORD hath made known his salvation: his righteousness hath he openly shewed in the sight of the heathen.

98.1.1.en: Christ declared His salvation by His Resurrection, and this appeared to the whole world, to the Gentiles as to the Jews, and He opened the door for everyone who accepts this declaration and believes in Him to receive salvation.

98.2.0.en: 3- He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel: all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.

98.2.1.en: 1- God gave many promises and prophecies in the Old Testament about His Incarnation and redemption, and in the fullness of time He remembered all these promises and fulfilled them by the Cross. For all the children of Israel who knew these prophecies, the way was made easy before them to believe in Christ, but the hardness of their hearts stood as an obstacle between them and faith, and they rejected the mercy of God and His salvation.

98.2.2.en: 2- The love of God appeared in delivering the good news of Christ the Redeemer to the whole world, even the lands far from Judea, and perhaps those far away at the ends of the earth are more concerned about faith and receiving salvation than many who are near, even the chosen people of God, who are the Jews who rejected faith.

98.2.3.en: May you praise God and sing to Him every day a new praise, for His works with you are renewed. So thank Him for His care and His keeping of you and His limitless love.

98.3.s.en: (2) How we rejoice in the Lord

98.3.0.en: 4- Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all the earth: make a loud noise, and rejoice, and sing praise.

98.3.1.en: David the prophet calls all the earth, Jews and Gentiles who have believed in Christ, to shout to the Lord for His salvation that He offered on the Cross, and he even encourages them to express their joy with all their abilities: they call out with loud voices, which is the joyful shout, and they sing words set to melody with their voices. And they also chant, that is, they proclaim melodious words accompanied by musical instruments. For he wants us to express our joy in God by every means and to glorify His wonderful salvation.

98.4.0.en: 5- Sing unto the LORD with the harp; with the harp, and the voice of a psalm. 6- With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King.

98.4.2.en: David calls the believers to express their joy, using musical instruments and every means of expressing joy, which are:

98.4.3.en: 1- The harp: a musical instrument with a set of stretched strings, and it symbolizes readiness, and the joining together of all a person’s powers and abilities to express thanks to God.

98.4.4.en: 2- The psalm: strong words that express a person’s joy, and it symbolizes zeal and spiritual earnestness.

98.4.5.en: 3- The trumpets and the sound of the cornet: these are instruments with loud sounds. The cornet is the horn of an animal that rises above its head, so it symbolizes the necessity of rising above bodily lusts in order to be free to praise God. The trumpets and the cornet symbolize the proclamation of the salvation of Christ and of the Holy Bible. All these praises and shouts we offer before the Lord the King, whom we want to reign over our hearts and purify us and satisfy us with His love.

98.4.6.en: Express your love for God by meditating on Him and by words of praise and by works of good, so that you declare your thanks to Him at all times.

98.5.s.en: (3) The joy of nature in the Lord

98.5.0.en: 7- Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

98.5.1.en: “Let roar”: the roaring is the loud sound of the waters of the sea.

98.5.2.en: 1- Nature shares in the praise of God its Creator, so the sea makes loud sounds as its waves collide, to declare its joy in God, and in this it joins the human beings who dwell in the whole earth, the believers in God who glorify His salvation.

98.5.3.en: 2- The sea symbolizes the world and those who dwell in it, who formerly made loud sounds to glorify lusts and evil, but now that they have believed they make praises and glorifications to Christ the Savior.

98.6.0.en: 8- Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together

98.6.1.en: 1- The rivers also join with the seas in rejoicing in God the Savior, for when the waters of the rivers crash they make sounds as if they were human hands clapping, declaring their joy. And the rivers symbolize the Apostles, servants and believers who overflow upon others with spiritual teachings and example by the power of the Holy Spirit, who flows from their bellies like rivers of living water (Jn 7:38).

98.6.2.en: 2- And the high mountains stand to sing without a voice; that is, by their appearance rising toward heaven they seem to praise God with the rest of creation. And the mountains symbolize the Apostles and the believers advanced in their spiritual lives, and the great servants who by their lives glorify the Savior.

98.7.0.en: 9- Before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity. All the displays of joy that men declare, and nature declares, are an offering before the Lord, who will judge the whole world on the day of judgment. So all the wronged, that is, the righteous who endured many pains for the sake of Christ, have their hope in the day of judgment, in which God judges with justice, and glorifies and compensates His righteous children with the glories of the Kingdom, and stands as a judge to judge with uprightness all the peoples of the earth.

98.7.1.en: Do not forget your goal, which is blessed eternity, where you will receive every blessing and God will compensate you for all your pains. So endure for His sake the toils of spiritual striving and service, and live in self-restraint and keep far from every evil, for God looks upon you with concern and never forgets your labor.

98.7.2.en: The Lord, the holy King: “The LORD reigneth; let the people tremble … v. 1”

98.7.4.en: 1- Its author: this psalm is considered one of the orphan psalms, that is, it has no title and its author is unknown, though some attribute it to David.

98.7.5.en: 2- This psalm is among the royal psalms, which are (Ps 95-100), and (Ps 93) is a preparation for them.

98.7.6.en: 3- There are three psalms that begin with “The LORD reigneth,” and they are (Ps 96, 97) and this psalm.

98.7.7.en: 4- This psalm tells us of the greatness of God, who reigned over His people in the Old Testament, and then in the fullness of time reigned on the Cross over the hearts of all who believed in Him in the whole world.

98.7.8.en: 5- This psalm prophesies about the Lord the Judge, who reigns on the day of judgment, and the peoples who did not believe in Him tremble before Him, because He punishes them, and at the same time He glorifies those who believe in Him.

98.7.9.en: 6- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Ninth Hour, in which Christ completed redemption on the Cross, because the psalm makes clear the reign of God over those who believe in Him and worship Him, whether from the Jews or the Gentiles, when He reigned on the wood of the Cross.
